eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Eleven
subtitle: Lesson 98 · Database Design Fundamentals

caption: Every column is nullable by default unless you say otherwise. No value, no row.

code:
-- Real AdventureWorks2012 constraint
ALTER TABLE dbo.Product
ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Product_ListPrice
CHECK (ListPrice >= 0.00);
caption: Goes beyond "is there a value?" — validates it against any boolean expression.

eyebrow: CHECK with a list of valid values
code:
-- Also real: Production.Product
ALTER TABLE dbo.Product
ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Product_Class
CHECK (Class IN ('L', 'M', 'H') OR Class IS NULL);
caption: Ranges, lists, pattern matching — any logic on that row, enforced on every INSERT and UPDATE.

eyebrow: No application code can bypass it
code:
INSERT INTO dbo.Product (ProductID, Name, ListPrice)
VALUES (1, 'Broken Widget', -5.00);
-- Msg 547: conflicted with CHECK constraint
-- "CK_Product_ListPrice"
caption: If even one code path forgets to validate, a CHECK constraint still catches it — every time.
